All 68 ordered source edge arrays equal V4 routing under converter mapping; endpoint/driver semantics are not proved by that comparison. All 278 reported render difference cells were investigated: 44 ED010 prefix rows (220 cells), 23 wire flags, 33 other row54 caption cells, a replacement glyph at [81,72], and final 4 of P.No 05703074. Parent inspected all native flag crops (with enlarged crops for row63), prefix rows, footer and row54 native tile. Row54 reads ED010 DR16-SEL08 P04-QP0-WD08 with damaged far endpoint; baseline has B and two replacement glyphs, and no terminal identity is inferred. SELECT15 [80,72]–[82,72], AF [198,22]–[199,22] and BD [176,31]–[177,31] have visible scan gaps; causes and route ownership unknown. All render differences remain unresolved. Two bounded read-only children sampled all 68 source nets spatially in original tiles, all 44 DRIVE target lead regions viewed; no first-half net established continuously. The second half's short outputs and AK received more direct visual attempts, while complex routes/branches remain ambiguous. Parent/children examined every 52 labelled junction neighborhood after expanding clipped panels; hollow marks are present, but precise ownership is unresolved. Two children viewed 20 direct native sheets containing 479 model contact candidates. Many panels are clipped or poorly localized; Resumed native coverage ledger flags known weak indices, not an exhaustive weak list. Such views do not adjudicate individual joins or prove original-only missing-wire absence. Exact electrical and source ownership, continuous branches, and omissions remain open. It cannot be independently read as BJ4 from this scan; neighboring BK4 does not establish it by sequence. Baseline TXT retains B and replacement characters; raw BJ.output and typed net 43 retain BJ4 as an unresolved source claim. The currently selected V4 and TXT differ from the historical baseline.
